A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiSCo/LPO research. All 19 pages, including Appendices A–I, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-security and code-generation evaluations, component and refinement ablations, and unseen-CWE generalization results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and analyses, including the experimental results in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The DiSCo distillation/refinement pipeline and two-stage SFT/LPO training remain unchanged, including security-token masking, reasoning and the regularizer (Sections 4–5; Appendix C).

E1.justification: Both versions use Python DiSCo training data, Security Eval, Asleep, LLMSecEval, DiSCo-Test, HumanEvalX and MBXP. The unseen-CWE evaluation scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same off-the-shelf, SafeCoder, SFT, DPO and SimPO methods. Table 2 retains GPT-4o-Mini, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet against Starcoder2 LPO.

E3.justification: The DiSCo split of 9,489/298/200, model configurations, training settings, generation temperatures, sample counts and evaluation metrics match throughout Section 6 and Appendices B, D, F and G.

E4.justification: The LPO component ablations, unseen-CWE test and refinement ablations in Tables 3–5 are unchanged. The CWE error analyses and overengineering examples in Section 8 and Appendices H–I are also retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains the same pass@k estimation procedure. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Starcoder2 LPO retains Security Eval InS of 11.4, I@100 of 20 and HumanEvalX P@1 of 38.9 in Tables 1–2.

T1.justification: The task definition, SFT/LPO equations, mask definitions and appendix mathematical explanations are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: security-informed preference-data distillation and localized preference optimization, with claimed improvements in code security and utility.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same security–utility tradeoff, overengineering and generalization interpretations. Limitations concerning synthetic-data noise, closed-source distillation, benchmark difficulty and Python-only evaluation are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data access statement, prompt templates, mask-computation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time and API-cost disclosures remain unchanged, including Appendices A, C and F.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The claimed distinction from prior secure-code training and preference-optimization methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first author's name expands from Mohammad Saqib to Mohammad Saqib Hasan, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The main-text and appendix wording, headings and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual inspection confirms the same Figures 1–5, Tables 1–6, prompt listings, captions and page organization. No figures or tables are added, removed, redrawn or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 expands the first author's name and updates the arXiv stamp while retaining the scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations and reproducibility information. These editorial updates produce no meaningful change in the paper's overall quality.
